claim: EU Council renewed Crimea/Sevastopol-related restrictive measures on 21 June 2021, including restrictions on investment and selected technology exports in transport, telecommunications and energy sectors.
limitations: Measures constrain specified channels; they do not quantify total Russian operational degradation.

claim: EU Council prolonged sectoral economic sanctions against Russia on 12 July 2021 through 31 January 2022, linked to non-implementation of the Minsk agreements.
limitations: Sanctions are a constraint signal, not proof of budget insufficiency or future military restraint.

claim: US Department of Defense publicly announced $125 million in security assistance for Ukraine on 1 March 2021.
limitations: Package value is not equivalent to deployed combat effectiveness.

claim: US Department of Defense publicly announced an additional $150 million in security assistance on 11 June 2021.
limitations: Capability conversion and delivery timing must be assessed separately.

claim: IEA later noted that it had already highlighted in September 2021 that Russia was reducing piped gas supplies to the EU and was not filling its EU storage sites to adequate levels.
limitations: Current page is a later synthesis referring back to a September 2021 warning; the underlying 2021 publication should be recovered before treating this as fully contemporaneous evidence.
